task.description:
Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0456, combined into this one handoff. ISS-0456's own filing text (docs/issues/ISS-0456.yaml) already CLAIMS this is the same recurring class as ISS-0418 (wasmex native-thread-pool exhaustion under CI contention, isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess) rather than ISS-0453 (a different mechanism -- poller_test.exs REQ-218 AC3 antagonist-contention test, MAIN suite not the isolated wasm_hang stage). Per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong' rule, this filing claim is NOT to be taken on trust just because it is already written down -- it was filed by ELIXIR-DEV mid-run under time pressure during a different run's Step Final CI wait, not by an agent whose job was to diagnose it. Your job is to INDEPENDENTLY VERIFY the match, not rubber-stamp the filing.

Do this concretely:
1. Read docs/issues/ISS-0418.yaml in full (already summarized for you in context.requirement_text below is NOT provided -- read the file directly, it is short) -- confirm its diagnosed mechanism (native WASM/wasmex Tokio thread-pool exhaustion inside the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` CI subprocess, manifesting as wall-clock timeout/ordering assertions pinned at their configured bound, or ExUnit.TimeoutError hangs inside Wasmex.start_link/start_instance) and its own recurrence_2026_09_03 field, which already documents a near-identical prior hit on test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_write_test.exs:460 with the exact same ExUnit.TimeoutError-after-180000ms-in-start_instance/2 shape ISS-0456 reports.
2. Read docs/issues/ISS-0453.yaml in full -- confirm it is a DIFFERENT mechanism (Letflow.Scheduler.Admission antagonist-contention race in poller_test.exs, MAIN suite, not the isolated wasm_hang stage) and that ISS-0456's failing tests (plugin_handler_test.exs, host_api_write_test.exs) do NOT match ISS-0453's file/subsystem/stage.
3. Confirm ISS-0456's own structural-clearing claim -- that PR #874's diff touched zero files under lib/letflow/engine/wasm/, test/letflow/engine/wasm/, lib/letflow/engine/lua/ -- is independently checkable from git history (git diff/git log against the merge commit named in the issue, or against the PR if still inspectable via gh) rather than accepted as written.
4. Reach an explicit verdict: does ISS-0456's failure signature genuinely match ISS-0418's already-diagnosed mechanism, or does it show something ISS-0418 does not already cover (e.g. a genuinely new failure shape, a new file, a mechanism ISS-0418's own text doesn't name)? State this as a real finding, not a restatement of the filing.
5. Do NOT implement any fix. Do NOT attempt to reproduce the CI-contention condition locally by brute-force running the isolated wasm_hang suite in a tight loop unless you judge it genuinely informative -- this class is documented (both ISS-0418 and ISS-0453) as CI-runner-contention-sensitive and not reliably reproducible on a quiet local machine; a clean local run proves little either way and is not required for this verdict. Prefer verifying via the CI run artifacts/logs already cited in ISS-0456's filing (run 33840184735, job 100920721979) if `gh run view`/`gh run view --log-failed` access is available, over a fresh local reproduction attempt.

Write your verdict into result.summary in enough detail for ORCH to decide the correct terminal status per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary (open/in_progress/resolved/instrumented/no_defect) WITHOUT re-deriving your reasoning -- ORCH will not re-open ISS-0418/ISS-0453 itself, it will read your verdict here.
acceptance_criteria: docs/issues/ISS-0418.yaml and docs/issues/ISS-0453.yaml both read in full and cited with specifics (not just their titles)

A stated, independently-derived verdict on whether ISS-0456 matches ISS-0418's mechanism, ISS-0453's mechanism, neither, or something new -- with the specific evidence (line numbers, error shapes, file paths) that supports it, not an assertion
PR #874's zero-touch claim on the wasm/lua paths independently checked, not inherited from the filing text
No fix implemented in this step
next_action names the correct next step given the verdict (fold into ISS-0418 / route to CODE-DESIGNER for a genuinely new root cause / other)

result.summary:
VERDICT: ISS-0456 genuinely matches ISS-0418's already-diagnosed mechanism (wasmex native Tokio thread-pool exhaustion in the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` CI subprocess). It shows NO shape ISS-0418 does not already cover, and it is structurally cleared from ISS-0453's mechanism (different subsystem/stage). Independently verified, not inherited from ISS-0456's own filing text.

1. ISS-0418 read in full. Its diagnosed mechanism: wasmex native Tokio thread-pool exhaustion inside the isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` CI subprocess (main suite always green, isolated stage flaky), manifesting either as a wall-clock-ordering assertion pinned at its configured bound, or as ExUnit.TimeoutError hangs inside Wasmex.start_link/start_instance. Its `recurrence_2026_09_03` field already documents a near-identical hit on host_api_write_test.exs:460 -- ExUnit.TimeoutError after 180000ms in start_instance/2, stack via :proc_lib.sync_start/2 -- the exact same file, exact same line number, and exact same stack shape ISS-0456 reports.

2. ISS-0453 read in full. Confirmed DIFFERENT mechanism: Letflow.Scheduler.Admission antagonist-contention race in test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs:575 (REQ-218 AC3), ran in the MAIN suite (CI run 33819989575, 'Result: 3191/3192 passed'), not the isolated wasm_hang stage. ISS-0456's failing files (plugin_handler_test.exs, host_api_write_test.exs, both under test/letflow/engine/wasm/) do not overlap ISS-0453's affected_files (test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs) or subsystem at all. No match.

3. PR #874's zero-touch claim independently checked via `gh pr view 874 --json files` (not inherited from the filing): the 22-file diff against main is entirely handoffs/, docs/issues/ISS-0451.yaml, lib/letflow/application.ex, lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md, lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, and test/letflow/supervisor/{pollers_breaker_test.exs,pollers_test.exs,infrastructure_test.exs}. Zero files under lib/letflow/engine/wasm/, test/letflow/engine/wasm/, or lib/letflow/engine/lua/ -- confirms ISS-0456's structural-clearing claim independently, not just via the filing's own `git diff --stat` narration.

4. CI log evidence independently pulled and read directly (`gh run view 33840184735 --json jobs` + `gh run view 33840184735 --log-failed`), not paraphrased from the issue file. Job 100920721979 ('Backend gate') failed at 05:38:43Z. Log line 339247 confirms this is the isolated `Including tags: [:wasm_hang]` stage, run separately after the main suite (which is not shown failing in this log excerpt -- the wasm_hang stage is a distinct `mix test --only wasm_hang` invocation per ISS-0418's own documented CI shape). Two failures read verbatim from the log:
  (a) test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs:474, 'REQ-170 AC4: the shorter configured timeout_ms binds sooner...' -- 'expected the 300ms-configured call (30000ms) to bind sooner than the 7_000ms-configured call (30000ms)' -- both elapsed times pinned at the outer 30000ms default, exactly ISS-0418's documented 'wall-clock-ordering assertion pinned at its configured bound' shape (compare ISS-0418's own PR #864 recurrence: plugin_handler_test.exs:355, 'took 30001ms' against a configured 500ms timeout_ms).
  (b) test/letflow/engine/wasm/host_api_write_test.exs:460, ** (ExUnit.TimeoutError) test timed out after 180000ms, code `start_instance("req172_write_then_hang.wat", ["var:write"])`, stacktrace via `(stdlib 8.0.3) proc_lib.erl:438: :proc_lib.sync_start/2` then `host_api_write_test.exs:66: ...start_instance/2` then `host_api_write_test.exs:461: (test)`. This is byte-for-byte the same file, same line number (:460), same 180000ms bound, and same :proc_lib.sync_start/2-inside-start_instance/2 stack shape as ISS-0418's own recurrence_2026_09_03 entry, which was the near-identical prior hit ISS-0418 itself already names.
  The Keycloak `econnrefused` log noise (repeated 'Metadata load failed for issuer ... Retrying in Nms') present throughout the log window is confirmed unrelated background retry noise (an OIDC metadata poller unconnected to WASM/Tokio), not the failure cause -- correctly characterized as 'concurrent unrelated noise' in ISS-0456's own filing, and this characterization is independently verified true (the failures' actual stacktraces contain no Keycloak/OIDC frames).

5. No fix implemented in this step, per WF-03 Step 1 and role restriction.

CONCLUSION: ISS-0456 is not a new root cause. It is the tenth-plus recurrence of ISS-0418's already-load-bearing, already-diagnosed wasmex native-thread-pool-exhaustion class, evidenced independently via direct CI log inspection rather than accepted from the filing's paraphrase. It does not match ISS-0453 (different file, different subsystem, different CI stage, confirmed by reading both issue records and cross-checking against ISS-0456's own affected_files). No genuinely new failure shape, no new file, no mechanism absent from ISS-0418's own text.
result.next_action: Do NOT route to CODE-DESIGNER as a fresh diagnosis. Fold ISS-0456 into ISS-0418: this instance adds no new mechanism, only another data point on an already-load-bearing, already-diagnosed defect (ISS-0418's OQ-5 concurrency-cap fix, per lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md section 8 and decision 0014, is still the correct and only structural fix). ORCH should close ISS-0456 at Step 5 as `status: instrumented` with `superseded_by: ISS-0418` (this diagnosis step did real, verified investigative work -- confirming zero-touch and matching the failure signature -- but removed no root cause; ISS-0418 already owns the fix), citing this handoff's evidence in the GitHub close comment, then release ISS-0456's queue_task_id (456) as done since the diagnostic work is complete and nothing further is owed on this issue specifically. Do NOT open a new WF-03 Step 2 fix-design run for ISS-0456 itself -- any future fix-design work belongs to ISS-0418's own queue entry (queue_task_id 418), not a new one.
